1.explanation: All of the rendering logic for the chevron and title lives in the AccordionItem component (and its helper defaultRenderExpando). To support an `align` prop you must modify AccordionItem’s render function—specifically, adjust the order of the `<ChevronRight16>` and `<div className="…__title">` (or apply a directional CSS class)—and update defaultRenderExpando/AccordionItem to accept and pass through the new `align` prop. No other files participate in rendering the chevron placement.
1.bug_scenario: The request is to add an `align` prop to Carbon’s AccordionItem so that the chevron icon can be aligned at the start of the heading (the new default) instead of always being at the end. The provided screenshot shows the chevron on the left side of “Section 1 title”, whereas the current implementation in AccordionItem always renders the Chevron icon after the title.

2.explanation: The core of this issue lives in AccordionItem.js. The AccordionItem component defines both the `defaultRenderExpando` function (which renders the `<button>` wrapper and the ChevronRight16 icon in a fixed order) and the main `AccordionItem` functional component itself. To add an `align` prop, you must update the AccordionItem signature, PropTypes, and its render logic: introduce an `align` prop (with values ‘start’ | ‘end’), adjust defaultRenderExpando (or the renderExpando usage) to swap the order of the Chevron and the title based on `align`, and then update the story (`Accordion-story.js`) and tests (`AccordionItem-test.js`) to demonstrate and verify the new behavior. These are the key elements that must be edited to support the new alignment feature.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a wrapped Carbon Accordion with each section’s chevron icon rendered on the left (“start”) of the heading rather than on the right (“end”), but the upstream AccordionItem component only renders the Chevron before the title in one fixed position. In other words, there is no `align` prop support in AccordionItem, so you cannot control whether the chevron appears at the start or end of the heading.
